Article Title: All eyes on Rohit Sharma in series decider at Lord's
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma

The mood inside the Indian dressing room must be difficult to read right now. Images from London showed head coach Gautam Gambhir sharing a laugh with Rohit Sharma on the Lord’s balcony on the eve of Sunday’s third ODI against England. Yet they could not mask the intense pressure the team’s oldest player must be under going into the series decider. The significance of the match extends far beyond another bilateral series. Its outcome could influence the team’s composition and planning over the next 15 months.The team management and selection committee have been ruthless in their decision-making over the past year, placing performance above a player’s stature and reputation. Yet uncertainty persists over how Rohit fits into India’s plans for the ODI World Cup in South Africa.Late on Friday, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said the 39year-old would “continue to represent India as long as he is in the scheme of things”. It is clear, however, that the selectors and management want to develop Yashasvi Jaiswal as an alternative opener. Another unconvincing outing on Sunday could dent Rohit’s hopes of playing in his fourth World Cup.After the England series, India’s next ODI is against West Indies in Trivandrum on Sept 27. Rohit has looked visibly uncomfortable against bounce and movement in England. Since stepping away from the other two formats, he has generally found form only late in a series, even at home.The official line within Indian cricket remains that there are few concerns about Rohit’s form. “It’s hard work with a new ball up front. We have seen that in the entire series. The ball is moving around. So batting up front, it is not easy. No doubt Rohit will work it out,” India’s fastbowling coach Morne Morkel said at the pre-match press conference on Saturday.
Article Summary: Rohit Sharma under intense pressure ahead of third ODI against England. The 39-year-old has looked visibly uncomfortable against bounce and movement. The outcome of the match could influence the team's composition and planning over the next 15 months. India’s next ODI is against West Indies in Trivandrum in September.

Article Title: PV Sindhu scripts history, beats Yamaguchi after four years to become first Indian to win Japan Open
Article Text:
PV Sindhu

Poll Vote & Share your view Which aspect of PV Sindhu's game impressed you the most during the Japan Open final? Her net play Her powerful smashes Her stamina in long rallies 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu defeated home favourite Akane Yamaguchi in straight games to win her maiden Japan Open title and first Super 750 crown in Tokyo on Sunday.The 31-year-old became the first Indian to win the Japan Open after beating the three-time world champion 21-17, 21-17. The victory ended her title drought of more than two years and marked her biggest title since winning the World Championships in 2019.Sindhu's previous title came at the Syed Modi International in 2024.Yamaguchi was playing her sixth Japan Open final, while Sindhu had not beaten the Japanese player in a completed match for four years. Their meeting at the Malaysia Open earlier this year ended after Yamaguchi retired following the opening game. Sindhu's last full-match win over her came at the Thailand Open in 2022.On Sunday, Sindhu stayed in control for most of the contest. Her net play played a key role as she repeatedly forced Yamaguchi to lift the shuttle before finishing points with cross-court and body smashes.Sindhu took an early 3-0 lead before Yamaguchi levelled the score at 3-3. The opening game remained close in the early stages, with both players exchanging points and errors.Sindhu moved ahead 8-6 after winning several points through her net play and extended the lead to 9-6 with a powerful smash. However, Yamaguchi fought back and went into the mid-game interval with a two-point advantage.After the break, Sindhu won a 36-shot rally to level the scores at 11-11 and quickly regained control. A cross-court smash, a net winner and a deep push helped her open a 16-12 lead.Yamaguchi narrowed the gap before both players produced a 38-shot rally at 17-15. The Japanese player eventually drew level, but Sindhu responded with two important points to move 19-17 ahead.Yamaguchi then hit the net before Sindhu closed out the opening game with a well-placed push into her opponent's backhand corner.Sindhu carried that momentum into the second game. She controlled the rallies from the front court and raced to an 8-3 lead after winning a 44-shot exchange.Although Yamaguchi reduced the gap to 8-7 after a few errors from Sindhu, the Indian recovered to lead 11-7 at the interval.Yamaguchi continued to struggle with her length and also lost a video challenge as Sindhu increased her lead to 14-7.The Japanese player made one final push to cut the deficit to 14-12, but Sindhu answered with two powerful smashes to move 17-14 and then stretched the lead further after another Yamaguchi error.Some late mistakes allowed Yamaguchi to close to 19-17, but the home favourite then hit wide to hand Sindhu three championship points.Sindhu sealed the title when Yamaguchi's final return landed long. The line call was confirmed after a video review.
Article Summary: PV Sindhu defeated Akane Yamaguchi in straight games to win her maiden Japan Open title and first Super 750 crown. The 31-year-old became the first Indian to win the Japan Open. The victory ended her title drought of more than two years.

Article Title: MLC 2026: LA Knight Riders clinch maiden title with thrilling one-run win over Washington Freedom
Article Text:
Image credit: Major League Cricket

Knight Riders post 164



Narine and Holder put LAKR in command



Pienaar almost steals the title



Shadley delivers under pressure



NEW DELHI: The Los Angeles Knight Riders held their nerve in a breathtaking final over to beat Washington Freedom by one run and win their maiden Major League Cricket (MLC) title at the Oakland Coliseum in California, California on Saturday.Needing 14 runs off the final over, Washington looked favourites after Obus Pienaar smashed the first ball for six. But Shadley van Schalkwyk produced three wickets in the last five deliveries, including a run-out off the final ball, to spark wild celebrations as the Knight Riders became MLC's newest champions.MI New York won the inaugural title in 2023 and again in 2025, while Washington Freedom lifted the trophy in 2024.Washington Freedom had won the toss and elected to bowl. Batting first, Los Angeles were bowled out for 164 in 19.4 overs.Andre Fletcher gave the innings early momentum with 47 off 27 balls, while Colin Munro made 40 off 29. After Andre Russell fell for a duck, Matthew Tromp played a crucial knock of 39 from 21 deliveries, striking three fours and three sixes.Washington kept fighting back with wickets at regular intervals.Ben Dwarshuis was the pick of the bowlers with 3/31, while Rachin Ravindra (2/23), Nikhil Chaudhary (2/32) and Mitchell Owen (2/14) chipped in to bowl the Knight Riders out.Washington Freedom never found early momentum in the chase as Sunil Narine ripped through the top order. The left-arm spinner removed Mitchell Owen (9), Steven Smith (8) and Rachin Ravindra (7) to finish with magnificent figures of 3/13.Captain Jason Holder then struck three important blows, dismissing Andries Gous (40), Nikhil Chaudhary (25) and Ben Dwarshuis (1), ending with 3/31.At 109/6 in the 16th over, the Knight Riders looked firmly in control.Pienaar launched a stunning counterattack, smashing 53 off just 24 balls, including three fours and five sixes, to drag Washington Freedom back into the contest.His half-century left Washington needing 14 runs from the final over, setting up a dramatic finish.The final over had everything. Pienaar started with a six over extra cover to bring the equation down to eight needed from five balls.Van Schalkwyk responded immediately with a perfect yorker that crashed into Pienaar's stumps, removing the set batter at the most crucial moment.The very next ball, Ian Holland tried to clear the infield but only managed to find Jason Holder at long-off, leaving Washington reeling.Lockie Ferguson then kept the chase alive with a boundary before taking a single, leaving Lahiru Milantha needing three runs off the final ball.Milantha completed the first run but was run out while attempting the second as wicketkeeper Jahmar Hamilton completed the dismissal, sealing a dramatic one-run victory for the Knight Riders.
Article Summary: Los Angeles Knight Riders beat Washington Freedom by one run. Obus Pienaar hit 53 off just 24 balls to drag Washington Freedom back into the contest. Shadley van Schalkwyk produced three wickets in the last five deliveries to spark wild celebrations.

Article Title: Before kick-off, Argentina vs Spain final has already entered FIFA World Cup history
Article Text:
Lamine Yamal and Lionel Messi (Image credit: Agencies)

Messi, Argentina chase history

Spain eye another record

Poll Vote & Share your view Which team has the better chance of breaking the defensive record? Argentina Spain Both have equal chances 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The FIFA World Cup 2026 final between Argentina and Spain will create history even before kick-off at the New York New Jersey Stadium on Sunday.It will be the first FIFA World Cup match featuring the world's top two ranked teams since the FIFA rankings were introduced in 1992, with Argentina entering the tournament as the No. 1-ranked side and Spain at No. 2.Argentina have also reached their seventh FIFA World Cup final, equalling Brazil for the second-most appearances in the title match.Only Germany, with eight finals, have played more.It is also Argentina's first appearance in consecutive World Cup finals since 1986 and 1990.The final pits Lionel Messi and defending champions Argentina against a Spain side that has not lost a match in 37 games, a run stretching back to early 2024.Spain are aiming to win their second FIFA World Cup after lifting the trophy in 2010. Argentina, meanwhile, are bidding to become the first men's team to win back-to-back World Cup titles since Brazil in 1958 and 1962.Spain coach Luis de la Fuente expects a memorable contest. "On Sunday, we will watch a great show. Two great national teams - two superteams, in my opinion - very similar in some aspects in terms of attitude, footballers' talent.I think that it's going to be an amazing final."Sunday's final will be Messi's first match against Spain since Argentina defeated the then world champions in an international friendly in 2010.The match will also see Messi share the field with Spain star Lamine Yamal, who was photographed with the Argentine legend as a baby nearly two decades ago.Spain head into the final after one of the best defensive campaigns in World Cup history.La Roja have conceded just one goal in seven matches and have not trailed for a single second during the tournament.If they win the title, they will better the defensive records set by Spain in 2010, Italy in 2006 and France in 1998, all of whom conceded only two goals while winning the World Cup.
Article Summary: Argentina face Spain in the FIFA World Cup 2026 final on Sunday. It will be the first time the top two teams in the world have met in a World Cup final. Lionel Messi and Argentina are bidding to win their second World Cup. Spain are aiming to break the defensive records set by Italy, France and Spain.

Article Title: 64-year-old record broken! England vs France rewrite FIFA World Cup history
Article Text:
AP Photo

Saka stars as England take control

Mbappe breaks Messi's World Cup scoring record

NEW DELHI: The FIFA World Cup 2026 third-place playoff between England and France entered the record books on Saturday as the teams produced a thrilling 10-goal contest.It was the first World Cup match in 64 years in which both teams scored four or more goals, since the Soviet Union and Colombia played out a 4-4 draw in 1962.It was also the highest-scoring World Cup match since Hungary's 10-1 win over El Salvador in 1982, while the 10 goals were the most ever scored in a World Cup third-place playoff.England eventually beat France 6-4 to claim the bronze medal.Bukayo Saka scored a hat-trick to inspire England's victory. He found the net in the 37th minute, first-half stoppage time and from the penalty spot in the 87th minute to register his second international hat-trick.Declan Rice opened the scoring before Ezri Konsa doubled England's lead, helping the Three Lions race to a 4-0 advantage by half-time.Jude Bellingham added the final goal in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time, taking his tournament tally to seven goals.The bronze medal is England's second-best finish at the FIFA World Cup after lifting the trophy in 1966.France mounted a strong fightback in the second half, with Kylian Mbappe scoring twice and Bradley Barcola and Ousmane Dembele also getting on the scoresheet.Mbappe's brace took his career FIFA World Cup tally to 22 goals, moving him past Lionel Messi's record of 21.The France captain also moved to the top of the Golden Boot standings with 10 goals, two ahead of Messi, who will have one more chance to add to his tally when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final.
Article Summary: England beat France 6-4 to claim the bronze medal at the FIFA World Cup 2026. It was the first World Cup match in 64 years in which both teams scored four or more goals. The 10 goals were the most ever scored in a World Cup third-place playoff.

Article Title: FIFA WC 2026: Kylian Mbappe crowns himself all-time World Cup king with record-shattering 14-goal campaign
Article Text:
France's Kylian Mbappe (10) reacts after scoring his side's third goal during the World Cup third-place playoff match between France and England. (AP Photo)

Kylian Mbappé has rewritten the history books of World Cup football, ascending to the absolute top of the FIFA World Cup 2026. Despite France suffering a dramatic 6-4 defeat to rivals England in Saturday’s third-place playoff, the French captain produced a statistical masterclass that cements his status as the most destructive attacking force the tournament has ever seen.By netting twice in the second half at the Hard Rock Stadium, the 27-year-old superstar moved to 10 goals for this edition, securing the Golden Boot. More historically, the double raised his career tally to an astonishing 22 goals, officially surpassing Argentina's Lionel Messi (21 goals) to become the leading World Cup goalscorer of all time.Mbappé’s historic evening did not stop at the goalscoring record. With his double against England, the French talisman reached a jaw-dropping 14 total goal involvements (goals and assists combined) in this 2026 edition alone. According to sports analytics giants Opta, this marks the highest number of goal involvements ever registered by a single player in one edition since detailed data tracking began in 1966.The staggering numbers showcase a campaign of sheer individual brilliance. Supported by a deadly partnership with winger Michael Olise, who also broke Pelé's tournament assist record, Mbappé single-handedly carried the creative and finishing responsibilities for Les Bleus across their fixtures in the United States.The historic milestone arrived during a chaotic second-half battle. Trailing 4-0 to an English side inspired by a Bukayo Saka hat-trick, Mbappé dragged his team back into the match. He beat Three Lions keeper Dean Henderson in the 48th minute before rifling home a fierce 14-yard strike in the 66th minute to break Messi's record and bring France within a single goal at 4-3.Ultimately, a sensational late solo goal from England’s Jude Bellingham sealed the 6-4 victory for the English, leaving France with the fourth position. While the team result brought immediate heartbreak, Mbappé leaves the United States having completely redefined modern football benchmarks. At just 27, the French speedster stands alone at the pinnacle of World Cup history.
Article Summary: Kylian Mbappé has rewritten the history books of World Cup football, ascending to the absolute top of the FIFA World Cup 2026. Despite France suffering a dramatic 6-4 defeat to rivals England in Saturday’s third-place playoff, the French captain produced a statistical masterclass. The 27-year-old superstar moved to 10 goals for this edition, securing the Golden Boot. More historically, the double raised his career tally to an astonishing 22 goals, officially surpassing Argentina's Lionel Messi (21 goals) to become the leading World Cup goalscorer of all time.

Article Title: Argentina equal Brazil's 24-year-old World Cup record, eye historic perfect title defence against Spain
Article Text:
Argentina's Lionel Messi (10) applauds the crowd during the World Cup. (AP Photo)

One win away from a flawless World Cup



Uruguay (1930) – 4 wins from 4 matches

Italy (1938) – 4 wins from 4 matches

Brazil (1970) – 6 wins from 6 matches

Brazil (2002) – 7 wins from 7 matches

Spain stand in the way of history



Defending champions Argentina stand on the brink of another slice of football history as Lionel Scaloni's side prepare to face Spain in the FIFA World Cup 2026 final, with a chance to set one of the game's rarest achievements while completing a remarkable title defence.The reigning champions have already equalled a 24-year-old World Cup record by becoming only the second team in history to win seven matches at a single edition of the tournament. The only other side to accomplish that feat was Brazil during their triumphant 2002 campaign in Japan and South Korea.Now, one more victory in Sunday's final at the New York New Jersey Stadium would elevate Argentina into an even more exclusive club.Argentina have won all seven of their matches en route to the final, defeating England 2-1 in a dramatic semifinal after coming from behind through goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez.Victory over Spain would make Lionel Messi and company only the fifth team in World Cup history to win every match on their way to lifting the trophy.Only four champions have previously achieved a perfect campaign:Argentina now have the opportunity to join those legendary teams while becoming the first nation since Brazil in 2002 to complete a flawless World Cup.They will also become first to win eight matches in one edition.Standing between Argentina and history is a confident Spanish side chasing their second World Cup title after their triumph in 2010.Luis de la Fuente's team has impressed throughout the tournament, conceding just one goal in seven matches while recording six clean sheets. Spain booked their place in the final with a composed 2-0 victory over France, thanks to goals from Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro.Ahead of the title clash, De la Fuente predicted an entertaining contest between two teams committed to attacking football."There are two top-class sides, two superb teams with many similarities... I think it's going to be a cracking match," the Spain coach said.Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni, meanwhile, insisted his side must produce its best performance despite their perfect run."We need to bring out our best version to try to win. We're a team that's already well-known by our rivals, and that's why it has double merit to have reached where we have. We'll try to win the final," Scaloni said.The Argentine coach also hailed Messi's extraordinary journey to another World Cup final at the age of 39."Having been able to reach a final the way Leo has... is incredible. We have to value what he does and the story and the legend that he is," Scaloni added.Sunday's final therefore offers far more than a battle for the trophy. For Argentina, it is an opportunity to equal Brazil's perfect 2002 campaign, complete back-to-back World Cup triumphs, and cement this generation's place among the greatest teams the sport has ever produced.
Article Summary: Defending champions Argentina face Spain in the FIFA World Cup 2026 final. Lionel Scaloni's side have won all seven of their matches on their way to the final. Victory over Spain would make them only the fifth team in World Cup history to win every match on the way to lifting the trophy. Only four champions have previously achieved a perfect campaign.

Article Title: FIFA World Cup Final: Lionel Messi's Argentina eye history, could become first team in 64 years to ...
Article Text:
PTI Photo

Messi vs Spain: A story comes full circle

Spain ready for biggest test

NEW DELHI: History will be on the line when Argentina face Spain in the FIFA World Cup 2026 final at the New York New Jersey Stadium on Sunday.Argentina are aiming to become the first men's team in 64 years to win back-to-back FIFA World Cup titles, after lifting the trophy in 2022.Only two nations have achieved the feat before - Italy (1934 and 1938) and Brazil (1958 and 1962).Spain, meanwhile, are chasing their second World Cup title after winning in 2010. They head into the final on an incredible 37-match unbeaten run stretching back to early 2024.Overall, Argentina have won six, drawn two and lost six matches against Spain in all competitions. Their only competitive victory came in the group stage of the 1966 FIFA World Cup, where they won 2-1.The final also brings together Lionel Messi and a country that played a huge role in his career. Born in Argentina, Messi spent part of his childhood and most of his club career in Spain. He was eligible to represent Spain internationally, but he always chose Argentina.Sunday's final will be his first match against Spain since a friendly in 2010, when Argentina defeated the then world champions.The match will also reunite Messi and Spain star Lamine Yamal, who famously appeared together in a photograph when Yamal was a baby.Despite the occasion, Messi said his approach remains unchanged."We grew up playing soccer with passion, eager to play. We played everywhere. We played on the street. We played at school. We played with teams. We didn't think about the pressure. It was just natural play."Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni had special praise for his captain."The best footballer that the world has seen."Later, Scaloni added: "He is pure history. History. A legend."Spain coach Luis de la Fuente believes the final will be a contest between two outstanding teams."On Sunday, we will watch a great show. Two great national teams - two superteams, in my opinion - very similar in some aspects in terms of attitude, footballers' talent. I think that it's going to be an amazing final."Spain captain Rodri also warned against focusing only on Messi."Argentina is far more than Messi. They've proven that they're a very complete team with top players. ... We are the best two teams playing in a collective manner as a group. Of course, we need to be mindful of Leo, but many other players."
Article Summary: Argentina face Spain in the FIFA World Cup 2026 final in New York on Sunday. Argentina are aiming to become the first men's team in 64 years to win back-to- back World Cup titles. Spain are chasing their second World Cup title after winning in 2010.

Article Title: FIFA WC 2026: Thunderstorms will clear wildfire smoke from New York haze ahead of World Cup final
Article Text:
The Statue of Liberty stands during sunset as smoke from wildfires blankets the sky, in the Brooklyn borough of New York. (AP/PTI)

In a major relief for football fans and organizers, severe thunderstorms passing through the Northeast United States are expected to clear the toxic Canadian wildfire smoke just in time for Sunday's mega World Cup final between Spain and Argentina at MetLife Stadium.Thick, gray smog had enveloped the region for days, triggering severe air quality warnings. On Saturday, heavy rain, booming thunder, and lightning lashed the open-air stadium, forcing state police to evacuate the seating bowl and field for shelter. The extreme weather even forced the Spanish national team to suspend their final pre-match training session due to safety concerns. FIFA officials confirmed they are monitoring the field conditions every ten minutes.However, meteorologists have brought good news, stating that the aggressive storm front will successfully "sweep the atmosphere clean" before the final kickoff. The air quality index in East Rutherford is predicted to improve from "unhealthy" on Saturday to a safe "moderate" level on Sunday."It won't be dangerous anymore. It's going to be dramatically better," said climate specialist Jeff Berardelli, adding that conditions for the match will be nearly perfect, with temperatures hovering around a pleasant 27 degrees Celsius, accompanied by low humidity and a light breeze.While the weather is clearing, a political storm has ignited over the environmental crisis. US President Donald Trump heavily criticized Canada on social media, accusing the neighbor of invading the US with "filthy, polluted, and unhealthy air" and threatening to impose new trade tariffs in retaliation.Canadian leaders hit back quickly. Ontario Premier Doug Ford called the tariff threats "absolutely unacceptable and shortsighted," pointing out that Canadian firefighters frequently help the US during natural disasters. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also weighed in, stating that global climate change is a shared responsibility. Currently, hundreds of unprecedented, lightning-triggered wildfires continue to burn across Canada, forced evacuations and scorching record amounts of land.
Article Summary: Thick, gray smog had enveloped the region for days, triggering severe air quality warnings. On Saturday, heavy rain, booming thunder, and lightning lashed the open-air stadium. The extreme weather even forced the Spanish national team to suspend their final pre-match training session due to safety concerns.

Article Title: Two Indian pacers to train with Australia's Test squad in Brisbane
Article Text:
Vasudev Prasad Singh, Abhishek Moond

Two young Indian fast bowlers, Abhishek Moond and Vasudev Prasad Singh, will train alongside Australia's Test squad next week.Abhishek Moond and Vasudev Prasad Singh are among a four-member MRF Pace Foundation delegation currently attending a two-week high-performance program at Cricket Australia's National Cricket Centre (NCC) in Brisbane from July 13 to 24.The delegation also includes former India fast bowler Tinu Yohannan and MRF Pace Foundation Program Manager and Head Coach M. Senthilnathan.The exchange is part of a development program that has linked the MRF Pace Foundation and Cricket Australia for more than three decades.The partnership dates back to 1992 and grew out of the association with Australian fast-bowling great Dennis Lillee, who played a key role in the development of the MRF Pace Foundation after it was established in Chennai in 1987.Over the years, the program has given young Indian cricketers the chance to experience Australian conditions and training methods, while Australian players have travelled to Chennai to prepare for subcontinental conditions.Although the partnership initially focused on fast bowling, it has gradually expanded into a broader high-performance exchange. In recent years, Australian batters, spinners and wicketkeepers have regularly trained at the MRF Pace Foundation to improve their game against spin and adapt to Indian conditions.Several leading cricketers have been associated with the program. Australian fast bowlers Glenn McGrath, Mitchell Johnson and Brett Lee have all spent time connected with the Foundation, while Indian cricket has benefited through the development of pacers such as Javagal Srinath, Zaheer Khan and several others who strengthened India's pace-bowling resources over the years.The exchange has also helped emerging Australian players gain overseas experience. Recent participants include Sam Konstas, Nathan McSweeney, Todd Murphy, Cooper Connolly, Josh Philippe, Ollie Peake, Corey Rocchiccioli, Joel Davies and Jason Sangha.The program will continue next month, with a Cricket Australia development squad set to visit the MRF Pace Foundation in Chennai from August 1 for a two-week training camp. Some of Australia's leading young players are expected to be part of the tour, continuing an exchange program that has supported player development in both countries for more than 30 years.
Article Summary: Abhishek Moond and Vasudev Prasad Singh will train alongside Australia's Test squad next week. The exchange is part of a development program that has linked the MRF Pace Foundation and Cricket Australia for more than three decades. The partnership dates back to 1992 and grew out of the association with Dennis Lillee.

Article Title: Farokh Engineer, Chandu Borde salute cricket’s ‘Kohinoor’ Sobers
Article Text:
Garfield Sobers

Mumbai : For Farokh Engineer , Sir Garfield Sobers was more than cricket’s greatest allrounder. He was a teammate, an opponent, a golfing partner and one of his closest friends. As the cricket world mourned the death of the West Indies legend at the age of 89 on Friday, the former India wicketkeeper remembered Sobers as a once-ina-lifetime cricketer whose genius remains unmatched.“I’m one of the few Indian cricketers who played against and with Sobers,” Engineer told TOI from Manchester. “No Indian player knew him better than I did. What a phenomenal man he was!” Engineer believes the debate over cricket’s greatest allrounder ends with Sobers. “We’ve had great batters like Sunil Gavaskar , Sachin Tendulkar and Dilip Vengsarkar, but Sobers was the most complete cricketer I’ve ever played with or against. He could bat, bowl left-arm pace, chinaman and orthodox spin, and field in the slips better than anyone.”Former India captain Chandu Borde , who faced Sobers through the 1950s and 1960s, echoed that sentiment. “I’m yet to come across a better allrounder than Sobers. He was the Kohinoor of cricket,” Borde said. “There used to be a celebration in our dressing room every time we dismissed him.”
Article Summary: Farokh Engineer remembers Sir Garfield Sobers as a once-ina-lifetime cricketer. Engineer believes the debate over cricket’s greatest allrounder ends with Sobers. Chandu Borde: “I’m yet to come across a better allrounder than Sobers”

Article Title: When Garry Sobers’ dropped chances helped Sunny!
Article Text:
Sunil Gavaskar, Garry Sobers

Garfield Sobers was the greatest allrounder of all time. Over 93 Tests, he smashed 8,032 runs, captured 235 wickets and snared 109 catches, some absolute gems in the slips. But during India’s 1971 tour to the Caribbean, the West Indian maestro dropped Sunil Gavaskar no less than three times, providing an inadvertent fillip to the career of the young opener playing his debut Test series. Gavaskar, who described Sobers as “the greatest cricketer I have ever seen” in his book ‘ Idols ’, detailed those missed chances in his autobiography ‘ Sunny Days ’.“I was glad to see Sobers grass a low fast edge off Holder as I tried to drive him off the back foot. Sobers tumbled in the attempt but spilled the ball. This was a lucky break,” he wrote. The chance was offered when Sunny was in his 20s and he went on to score 65 on debut. It was the same Test where India recorded their first -ever win against West Indies in Trinidad. Sobers also had a hand, literally, in Gavaskar getting his first ton. The opener wrote, “As I was nearing my first century, dark clouds began gathering and it started to drizzle. Play continued, however, and on 94 I survived what was probably the simplest of catches.”It transpires that Sunny played forward to a flighted delivery from off-spinner Jack Noreiga.“The ball spun and jumped, hitting me on my glove and went to Sobers, who would have taken a dolly if he had been standing where he was before the ball was delivered. But Garry, anticipating my forward defensive stroke, had moved forward,” wrote Gavaskar. Sobers missed the grab. “At the end of the over, Gary stood in front of me and said, ‘Maan, why are you after me, can’t you find some other fielder?’ He had dropped me thrice so far and this last one was the easiest of the lot. ” Sunny went on to score 116.But the West Indian great took everything in stride. Gavaskar scored 124 and 220 in the last Test, taking his run tally to a staggering 774 in the series. “As I walked back to the pavilion, Sobers smilingly tousled my cap,” wrote Sunny. The two cricketers were on the same side, Rest of the World, against Australia in 1971-72. Sobers’ 254 against Lillee and Co. in Melbourne was described by Donald Bradman as “the greatest ever since the War”. And yet “the remarkable thing is that he never wore a thigh guard in his life,” wrote Sunny.
Article Summary: Garry Sobers dropped Sunil Gavaskar no less than three times during India's 1971 tour to the Caribbean. Sobers' 254 against Lillee and Co. in Melbourne was described by Donald Bradman as ‘the greatest ever since the War’

Article Title: With retirement rumours swirling, Rohit Sharma turns up for optional practice at Lord's
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma (PTI Photo)

TimesofIndia.com in London:

There were plenty of chants as Rohit Sharma walked into the iconic Lord's cricket ground on Saturday. The mood remained the same as he walked out nearly three hours later."The most important man in all of India!" yelled one fan. Another declared, "Ek century pakka kal! (One century tomorrow for sure!)," as Rohit smiled and took his place in the luxury black bus. The runs may not be flowing for the 'Hitman'. The naysayers may be pushing him out of the side rather than backing him to stay. But fans do not see things that way.Rohit Sharma has scored 891 runs since the start of 2025, behind Shubman Gill 's 974 and Virat Kohli 's 961. This year, he has scored 241 runs, behind Gill's 484 and Kohli's 310. The pressure, even if the team management denies it, must be playing a role.As Rohit and Kohli prepare for what could be their last bilateral game in England, their contributions to the game have not been forgotten."They've obviously been phenomenal players for many years, and it's good to see them still playing the game," England skipper Harry Brook said ahead of the third ODI, with the series locked at 1-1.Rohit has scored only 37 runs in the ongoing series, 11 in Birmingham and 26 at Cardiff, prompting questions over whether the 39-year-old's place in India's ODI team is under threat.Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak insisted there was no pressure to speak of.On Saturday, Morne Morkel added another proverbial arm around Rohit's shoulder."It is hard work with the new ball upfront. We have seen that throughout the series. The ball is moving around."So batting upfront is not easy. No doubt Rohit will work it out. He has done it in the past. He is experienced, and he brings calmness to the batting line-up. So, without a doubt, there are no worries or concerns at all about the way he is going about things," the South African added.His record at Lord's does not inspire much confidence. The right-hander has played five matches at the venue and scored just 133 runs, including an 83 in a Test in 2021. In four white-ball matches, he has managed only 29 runs, with a top score of 15 in 2018. In fact, his last outing here ended in a 10-ball duck as England thrashed India by 100 runs.Hoping to change that, Rohit took part in the optional practice session ahead of the third ODI alongside Ishan Kishan , KL Rahul, Kuldeep Yadav and Prince Yadav.During a batting stint that lasted just over an hour, Rohit faced Kuldeep, Mayank Yadav and the sidearm specialists. He looked largely in good touch and in control. During breaks, he joked and laughed with members of the support staff. After finishing, he walked to the bench, took off his gear and had a lengthy chat with coach Gautam Gambhir . Even before the nets session, Rohit was seen standing alongside Gambhir and Kotak on the Lord's balcony, sharing a hearty laugh.Even if this turns out to be the last ODI of Rohit Sharma's illustrious career, the crowd will undoubtedly turn up in large numbers for one final glimpse of one of India's greatest white-ball cricketers at one of the game's most iconic venues.
Article Summary: Rohit Sharma has scored only 37 runs in the ongoing series, 11 in Birmingham and 26 at Cardiff. His last outing here ended in a 10-ball duck as England thrashed India by 100 runs. The 39-year-old took part in an optional practice session ahead of the third ODI.

Article Title: 'Nobody can come close to him': Kapil Dev hails Sir Garfield Sobers as cricket's greatest all-rounder
Article Text:
Sir Garfield Sobers and Kapil Dev

'We had all-rounders, but not on his scale'



The man who changed cricket's thinking



NEW DELHI: Sir Garfield Sobers was much more than a legendary all-rounder — he was the cricketer who revolutionised the game and changed how future generations approached it, former India captain Kapil Dev said while paying tribute to the West Indies great following his death at the age of 89.Speaking to PTI on Saturday, Kapil described Sobers as one of the finest cricketers ever to grace the sport, saying his influence stretched far beyond statistics and records."I think anybody who knows about cricket should know about Gary Sobers. One of the finest cricketers ever born on this earth," Kapil said. "The way he played cricket inspired people like us. It's a sad day. He's no more, but he's given us so much — so much cricket and his talent and ability which we follow throughout our lives."Sobers, widely regarded as the greatest all-rounder in cricket history, passed away at his home in Barbados on Friday, just 10 days before his 90th birthday.Kapil, himself one of cricket's greatest all-rounders, believes no player has ever matched Sobers' extraordinary versatility."I think, well, we had all-rounders, but not on his scale. I don't think anybody can come close to him, the way he played batting, bowling, fast bowling, spin bowling, fielding.Everything — he had the ability and the knack for entertaining. At the end of the day, many cricketers will emerge, but very few will be true entertainers," Kapil said.According to Kapil, Sobers' greatest gift was not just his immense talent but the joy with which he played the game."I think it's the talent, the way he used to enjoy himself and the way he used to play. During that era, no doubt the West Indies team was one of the best, but he set records and shifted people's mindset of how to play and enjoy," he added.Kapil recalled how Sobers challenged the conventional coaching philosophy of his time and inspired young cricketers to think differently."The biggest thing I remember is that he changed the method of MCC cricket coaching, what we used to call playing in 'V'," he said. "I think the first thing I came to know is not playing V, how you can get runs. That was the biggest statement stuck in my mind when I was growing up."Kapil also remembered Sobers as a warm personality away from the cricket field."He was a brilliant cricketer. We lost him, but one can learn from the way he played cricket. Hats off to him, as he just enjoyed his life. In the evening, he used to sit and talk and we were just good listeners. He talked more about other things in life rather than cricket," he added.Sobers' career remains one of the most extraordinary in cricket history. He scored 8,032 Test runs at an average of 57.78, claimed 235 wickets, smashed a then-world record 365 not out against Pakistan in 1958, and became the first batter to hit six sixes in an over in first-class cricket in 1968. Knighted in 1975, the Barbados legend also has the ICC's premier men's individual honour — the Sir Garfield Sobers Award — named after him, ensuring his legacy will continue to inspire generations of cricketers.
Article Summary: Kapil Dev pays tribute to Sir Garfield Sobers, one of cricket's greatest all- rounders. Former India captain says Sobers changed the way cricketers played the game. Sobers passed away at his home in Barbados on Friday, just 10 days before his 90th birthday.

Article Title: 'Do we need Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma?': R Ashwin breaks silence on India's 2027 World Cup plans

Amid speculation over Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli's ODI futures, former India off-spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has questioned the timing of the debate, insisting that if the selectors wanted to move on from the veteran duo ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup, they should have communicated that decision much earlier.In recent weeks, social media has been abuzz with speculation that either Rohit Sharma or Virat Kohli could be dropped from India's ODI plans before the 2027 World Cup. Media reports even claimed that the third ODI at Lord's could be Rohit's final appearance in the format.However, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia dismissed those rumours while speaking to PTI on Friday, confirming that Rohit will continue to represent India in ODIs and rubbishing the speculation surrounding his retirement."There are lot of speculations going on in media about Rohit Sharma's future. I want to firmly assert that there has been no such discussion that Rohit will be playing his last match at Lord's on Sunday," said Saikia, as quoted by PTI.Speaking on his YouTube channel Ash Ki Baat, Ashwin said India still needs the experience of Rohit and Virat for the upcoming tour of South Africa, but stressed that if the team management had decided to move on from them, the players should have been informed immediately after the Champions Trophy rather than allowing uncertainty to linger."I am thinking we are going to South Africa in September and October. Do we need Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma? If you ask me, I will say we need that experience. I know Yashasvi Jaiswal is pushing hard from behind, but if you ever felt as a selector, coach or captain that we don't want these players in the 2027 World Cup, then you could have communicated that at the end of the Champions Trophy," Ashwin Said.Ashwin, who himself retired from international cricket after being informed that the team management wanted to look beyond him, said honest communication is essential when dealing with senior players."If you go to a player and tell him that we want to move on from you, no player will like that. Even when the coach came and communicated with me in Australia that they wanted to look past me, I accepted it. One bad series can happen to any player, but you have to communicate with the player."The 39-year-old also questioned why such discussions are surfacing now, with less than a year remaining before the 2027 ODI World Cup."Beyond all the speculation, Rohit and Virat have been performing. If you really wanted to make such a transition, why has this discussion come only now, in August 2026, when there are only 10 to 12 months left before the Cricket World Cup?"

Article Title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Final: Lionel Messi's Argentina aim to accomplish in New York what Diego Maradona couldn't in Rome 36 years ago
Article Text:
Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona (Image credit: Agencies)

Argentina, Spain set for blockbuster final



NEW DELHI: Argentina have already achieved a major milestone before taking the field for the FIFA World Cup 2026 final against Spain at the at New York New Jersey Stadium on Sunday.The defending champions have reached their seventh FIFA World Cup final, equalling Brazil for the second-most final appearances in tournament history.Only Germany, with eight finals, have appeared in more title matches.It is also the first time since Diego Maradona inspired Argentina to back-to-back World Cup finals in 1986 and 1990 that the country has reached consecutive title matches. Argentina won the World Cup in 1986 before finishing runners-up in 1990. Their seven final appearances have come in 1930, 1978, 1986, 1990, 2014, 2022 and 2026.Now, Lionel Messi and Argentina have the chance to become the first men's team to win back-to-back FIFA World Cup titles since Brazil achieved the feat in 1958 and 1962.The final will pit defending champions Argentina against a Spain side that is unbeaten in 37 matches, a run stretching back to early 2024.Spain are chasing their second FIFA World Cup title after winning in 2010, while Argentina are looking to successfully defend the trophy they won in Qatar four years ago.Spain coach Luis de la Fuente believes fans are in for a memorable contest."On Sunday, we will watch a great show. Two great national teams - two superteams, in my opinion - very similar in some aspects in terms of attitude, footballers' talent. I think that it's going to be an amazing final."The 104th and final match of the biggest FIFA World Cup ever, featuring 48 teams across the United States, Canada and Mexico, will decide whether Argentina retain their title or Spain lift the trophy for the second time.
Article Summary: Argentina have reached their seventh FIFA World Cup final, equalling Brazil for the second-most final appearances in tournament history. Only Germany, with eight finals, have appeared in more title matches. First time since Diego Maradona inspired Argentina to back-to-back World Cup finals in 1986 and 1990 that the country has reached consecutive title games.

Article Title: For the first time in 96 years, FIFA unveils special award ahead of Spain vs Argentina World Cup final
Article Text:
FIFA unveils historic World Cup championship rings (Image: X)

Spain vs Argentina: A final for the ages

For the first time in the 96-year history of the FIFA World Cup, the champions will be awarded exclusive FIFA World Cup Championship Rings, adding a new symbol of glory alongside the iconic trophy. The rings will make their debut after the FIFA World Cup 2026 final between Spain and Argentina, scheduled for Sunday, July 19, at the New York New Jersey Stadium (MetLife Stadium) in East Rutherford.One side of the championship ring features the iconic FIFA World Cup Trophy, while the other will be custom-designed to reflect the identity of the winning nation. FIFA has also unveiled a limited-edition collection of 2,026 rings, with 30 reserved for the World Cup winners and the remaining 1,996 made available to fans worldwide.Immediately after the final, the winning team's captain and head coach will receive temporary championship rings during the on-field celebrations. The final versions of the 30 winners' rings will later be individually custom-made and officially presented, ensuring a personalised fit and creating a lasting keepsake of their World Cup triumph.The FIFA World Cup 2026 final will kick off at 3:00 PM local time (12:30 AM IST on Monday, July 20), with Spain and Argentina battling for football's biggest prize, and the inaugural championship rings.The showdown also features a captivating generational storyline as 39-year-old Lionel Messi prepares to face 19-year-old Lamine Yamal in their first-ever competitive meeting. The clash has generated worldwide interest, fuelled by the rediscovered 2008 charity photoshoot in which a 20-year-old Messi posed with a baby Yamal in a bathtub at Camp Nou, a moment that has since become one of football's most iconic images.Argentina booked their place in the final with a dramatic 2-1 comeback victory over England, ending the Three Lions' hopes of reaching their first World Cup final since 1966.Spain, meanwhile, secured their first World Cup final appearance since lifting the trophy in 2010 by defeating France 2-0 in a composed semifinal display.
Article Summary: FIFA unveil exclusive FIFA World Cup Championship Rings. The rings will make their debut after the 2026 final between Spain and Argentina. 30 rings will be reserved for the World Cup winners and the remaining 1,996 made available to fans worldwide. The final versions of the 30 winners' rings will later be individually custom-made and presented.

Article Title: Beyond football: Why Spain vs Argentina is also a clash of politics
Article Text:
A fan waves an Argentine flag at the Obelisk while Argentina faces Austria for a World Cup football match in Buenos Aires, Argentina, Monday, June 22, 2026. (AP Photo)

Amidst the rubble in Gaza, and away from the spectacle of the FIFA event in North America, a simulation World Cup game was played on Thursday among the footballers who have survived the ongoing “genocide” in Palestine.It was a surreal sight that looked right out of a Polanski war film.The green turf, surrounded by a city in a shambles, was not just witness to the first football game to be live streamed in Gaza since the Israel-led attacks began in Oct 2023, the six-a-side game also had an interesting political context.While one team was in Palestine national colours, the other had on them the Spanish jersey — apparently in acknowledgement of Spain’s support and recognition of the state of Palestine. It also brought to fore the support that the La Rojas would garner from this strife-torn region when they face off against Argentina in the World Cup final on Monday.The Spanish flags that were fluttering beside the Palestinian ones were also testimony to the fact that despite all the mandates from FIFA to make the World Cup free of politics, the reality was far from the rules written behind closed doors of its Zurich headquarters.It also doesn’t help the Gianni Infantino-led world body’s cause that the protagonists at the MetLife Stadium on Monday will be representing two countries on opposite ends of the political spectrum.While Spain’s socialist prime minister Pedro Sanchez has been the loudest voice for Palestine, inclusiveness and left ideology in Europe, his Argentine counterpart’s political ideology can be summed up in him being one of the strongest supporters of US President Donald Trump Prime minister Javier Milei has been famously quoted as saying that “the only left that works is the left foot of Messi”.He is an anarcho-capitalist, minarchist and libertarian conservative, who advocates conservative social values, is an Israel supporter and has Benjamin Netanyahu as another famous friend.That his ideology may have spilled over to the World Cup venues is evident in the racist slurs that some Argentine fans have been documented as inflicting on a coloured US influencer as well as them throwing beer on Egypt fans during Argentina’s round of 16 clash.There was the incident of some players from the 2022 World Cupwinning team singing a racist song on the team bus after their victory in Qatar.It is a satire on history itself that the country once colonised by the Spanish empire — that rid the land of its own people — now has Milei’s rightist govt at the helm while its colonisers are standing to the left and advocating for diversity and socialism. And, that the Latin American finalists are the only all-white team among the 48 nations at the World Cup while Spain will have players of immigrant descent like Lamine Yamal and Nico Williams working in tandem with ethnic Spaniards like Pedri and Ferran Torres to bring the trophy home.It is also worth noting that the man who has replaced the Che-tattoo sporting Maradona as football’s greatest, remains apolitical, seeing nothing in being seen with Trump. Hence, Lionel Messi is also in stark contrast to his striking counterpart at the opposite end, the 19-year-old Yamal, who waved the Palestinian flag during Barcelona’s victory parade.And that’s the reality the world will stare at when the summit clash kicks off in New Jersey.However, the 2026 edition — being held in the backdrop of the US and Israel’s war on Iran — has already been mired in politics.While the Iran team had to shift its base to Mexico due to US sanctions and forced to rush in and out of the States for its matches, the African Referee of the Year, Somalian Omar Artan, was victim to another of the hosts’ sanctions preventing him from entering its lands to officiate at the World Cup.So, when the La Rojas take the field against the Albiceleste, the political overtones will linger in its background.And while a Spanish victory is bound to see the La Rojigualda flutter in the far-off Gaza sky, an Argentine win will not just be another gift for Messi fans but is also likely to make the biggest icons of the right wing — Milei, Trump and Netanyahu, who has also expressed his support for Argentina — rejoice in unison.
Article Summary: A simulation World Cup game was played on Thursday among the footballers who have survived the ongoing ‘genocide’ in Palestine. While one team was in Palestine national colours, the other had on them the Spanish jersey. It also brought to fore the support that the La Rojas would garner from this strife-torn region when they face off against Argentina in the World Cup final on Monday.

Article Title: The Argentines in Spain : La Roja’s biggest headache
Article Text:
Argentina's Lionel Messi, left, celebrates with Rodrigo de Paul after scoring the opening goal against Cape Verde during the World Cup round of 32 football match in Miami Gardens, Fla., Friday, July 3, 2026. (AP Photo)

LIONEL MESSI

RODRIGO DE PAUL

GIOVANNI LO CELSO

NAHUEL MOLINA

JULIAN ALVAREZ

GIULIANO SIMEONE

GONZALO MONTIEL

Other players with La Liga links:

Argentina and Spain share a long football relationship, with some of the most iconic players of the Latin American giants plying their trade in La Liga. Starting from Alfredo de Stefano in the 1950s to Mario Kempes, Diego Maradona, Jorge Valdano and Leo Messi, Argentina’s elite has been part of Spanish football architecture. While some bring the Latin American finesse, the others import the tough neversay-die attitude, something that has gone into the DNA of La Roja too.TOI takes a look at the top Argentinian players in Spanish clubs who are now looking to scupper Spain’s charge for their second World Cup title.The boy from Rosario is synonymous with FC Barcelona. Joining the La Masia academy at the age of 13 in 2000, he spent the next 21 years at the club, establishing himself as the player that he is today, winning 35 titles with the Catalans. However due to Barca’s financial problems, he had to leave in 2021. The Spanish FA even tried to convince Messi to declare for Spain when he was a youngster, but Messi chose to play for Argentina.One of the established members of the squad, the defensive midfielder spent four years at Atletico Madrid between 2021-25. Moving from Italian club Udinese, De Paul quickly established himself as one of the most reliable midfielders in Argentine great Diego Simeone’s team and gave a torrid time to the elite of Spain and Europe.He is at Inter Miami now.Despite spending a chunk of his career playing in England, Lo Celso’s spell in Spain can’t be ignored. First moving to Real Betis on loan from PSG, the midfielder has also played for Villarreal and is now back with Manuel Pellegrini’s team that finished fifth and qualified for Champions League this season.Molina is one of Argentina’s most reliable fullbacks. Molina made the move to Atletico from Udinese. Under Simeone, Molina has become a key part of Atleti’s defensive might. He scored his first goal for Argentina in the 2022 World Cup QFs against the Netherlands.After his move to Atletico Madrid in 2024 from Manchester City, the shining light of new-age Argentina has won many matches for Simeone’s side. His ability to break open tough defences is something that has helped him become a mainstay for Atletico, who are fighting tooth-and-nail to keep the player in their team as Barcelona are going all out for him.Giuliano, the son of Atletico Madrid coach Diego, is another crucial member of the club who played an important role for Argentina against England. The rightsided attacking midfielder combines the feistiness and the flair that’s common to both Atletico and Argentina.The defender, who took Argentina’s World Cup winning penalty in 2022, spent four years at Sevilla, and with whom he won the 2023 Europa League, beating Roma in the final. In the semifinal against England, he came on in the 71st minute and played an important role in Argentina making the final.Reserve goalkeepers Geronimo Rulli (Sociedad and Villarreal), Juan Musso (Atletico Madrid), Nico Paz (Castilla and Real Madrid), midfielders Thiago Almeda and Nico Gonzalez (Atletico Madrid) have been integral parts of Spanish club football.
Article Summary: Argentina and Spain share a long football relationship, with some of the most iconic players of the Latin American giants plying their trade in La Liga. Starting from Alfredo de Stefano in the 1950s to Mario Kempes, Diego Maradona, Jorge Valdano and Leo Messi, Argentina’s elite has been part of Spanish football architecture.

Article Title: 13 matches and counting! Lionel Messi's Argentina become the first team ever to ...
Article Text:
Argentina's Lionel Messi (AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)

Argentina will carry remarkable attacking momentum into the FIFA World Cup 2026 final against Spain after becoming the first team in tournament history to score at least two goals in 13 consecutive World Cup matches.Lionel Scaloni's side extended the record with a dramatic 2-1 comeback victory over England in the semifinals, making it 13 straight World Cup games with two or more goals.The streak began after Argentina's shock 2-1 defeat to Saudi Arabia in their opening match of the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar, the last time the Albiceleste failed to score at least twice in a World Cup fixture.Argentina have also found the net in 16 successive World Cup matches, placing them among the competition's greatest attacking teams. Only Hungary (17 matches between 1934 and 1962), Germany (18 between 1934 and 1958 and again from 1986 to 1998), and Brazil (18 between 1930 and 1958) have produced longer scoring streaks.Now, the defending champions will look to continue that remarkable run when they take on UEFA Euro 2024 winners Spain in Sunday's final at New York New Jersey Stadium.Argentina reached the title clash after overturning a first-half deficit against England.Enzo Fernandez levelled the scores before Lautaro Martinez struck a stoppage-time winner to send the reigning champions into a second successive World Cup final.Spain, meanwhile, advanced with a composed 2-0 victory over France. Mikel Oyarzabal converted a penalty earned by teenage sensation Lamine Yamal before Pedro Porro added a second after the break, while Spain's defence secured its sixth clean sheet in seven tournament matches.Spain coach Luis de la Fuente expects "a cracking match" between two sides committed to attacking football, while Scaloni believes Argentina must produce their "best version" to retain the title.The Argentina coach also praised 39-year-old Lionel Messi for reaching yet another World Cup final, calling his longevity and influence "incredible".With history, records and the biggest prize in world football on the line, Argentina's prolific attack will once again be under the spotlight.
Article Summary: Argentina are the first team in tournament history to score at least two goals in 13 consecutive World Cup matches. The streak began after Argentina's shock 2-1 defeat to Saudi Arabia in their opening match of the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar. Argentina reached the title clash after overturning a first-half deficit against England. Spain, meanwhile, advanced with a composed 2-0 victory over France.

Article Title: Travis Hunter’s wife finally addresses the viral cheating rumor that has followed her for nearly two years
Article Text:
Travis Hunter’s wife finally addresses the viral cheating rumor that has followed her for nearly two years (Instagram)

Leanna Lenee says the viral story had nothing to do with Travis Hunter

Leanna Lenee has heard the rumors for long enough. Nearly two years after old videos and photos sparked cheating allegations online, the wife of Jacksonville Jaguars rookie Travis Hunter has finally shared her side of the story. In a TikTok video posted in July 2026, Lenee denied the claims and explained why she believes the internet built a false narrative around her past.The controversy first exploded in December 2024, just days after Hunter won the Heisman Trophy. While much of the attention should have stayed on the Colorado star's historic achievement, social media quickly shifted its focus to Lenee. Old content resurfaced, criticism snowballed, and cheating rumors spread across several platforms. Now, she has directly responded.Speaking in a TikTok video, Lenee made it clear that she never cheated on Travis Hunter and challenged the narrative that has followed her since 2024. "The funniest part about this comment is like I literally never cheated," Lenee said in the TikTok video. She explained that the rumors started after people dug through her past while reacting to criticism she received during Hunter's Heisman Trophy celebration in December 2024.According to Lenee, an old party photo with another man became the center of the story even though, as she described it, the interaction lasted "maybe max 10 minutes." She claimed the moment had nothing to do with Hunter and happened only because she wanted to make her ex-boyfriend jealous.She also said the timing of the incident matters because she and Hunter were not together then. "I hadn't met him in person at that time, definitely wasn't dating him," Lenee said in the same TikTok video. She added that she never spoke to the man again and accused him of chasing "15 minutes of fame" after the clip resurfaced online.The video she referenced became a major talking point in December 2024. According to Page Six, the footage allegedly showed Lenee dancing with a man while wearing a schoolgirl outfit. Although her face was not visible, the outlet reported that viewers linked the person in the video to Lenee because of a visible thigh tattoo and photos she had previously shared wearing the same outfit.TMZ later reported that the footage was from several years earlier, before Lenee and Travis Hunter began their relationship. While neither outlet confirmed the exact date of the recording, both indicated that the clip predated the couple's romance.In late 2024, as the online backlash intensified, both Travis Hunter and Lenee temporarily deactivated their Instagram accounts. The criticism continued for months, but neither publicly addressed the cheating allegations in detail until now.Despite the constant online attention, the couple's relationship moved forward. Travis Hunter proposed before they married in May 2025, and they welcomed their first child in August 2025.Travis Hunter has rarely commented on the criticism directed at his wife, but he has consistently stood by her amid the public scrutiny. Lenee's latest TikTok marks her clearest response yet, as she firmly rejects the cheating allegations and insists the viral story never reflected what actually happened.
Article Summary: Leanna Lenee says she never cheated on Travis Hunter. In a TikTok video posted in July 2026, Lenee denied the claims and explained why she believes the internet built a false narrative around her past. The controversy first exploded in December 2024, just days after Hunter won the Heisman Trophy.

Article Title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce face a honeymoon race against time as NFL training camp approaches
Article Text:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce honeymoon plans (Getty Images)

What are Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift's honeymoon plans?

Is Travis Kelce ready for the 2026 Chiefs season?

Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift have kept things quiet since their July 3 wedding at Madison Square Garden, but that's about to change in the biggest way possible. The newlyweds are reportedly planning an ambitious around-the-world honeymoon spanning the Caribbean, Europe, Asia, and Australia and they're doing it all before Kelce reports to Kansas City Chiefs training camp in late July. A brief Montana stay and a trip to California for JuJu Smith-Schuster's wedding have been the extent of their post-nuptials so far.The scale of what the couple has in mind is striking. According to a source who spoke to The Sun, Kelce and Swift have been coordinating this for weeks and have already told their inner circle not to expect to hear from them. "Unless there is an emergency, they want to limit outside contact to truly immerse themselves in this once-in-a-lifetime experience," the source said.The list of destinations is genuinely ambitious for a trip squeezed into a matter of weeks. The Caribbean, Europe, Asia, Australia -- it reads less like a honeymoon itinerary and more like a world tour. Which, in a way, makes perfect sense for two people whose schedules have been defined by exactly that.The source added that the trip is about something simpler than the spectacle. "It's a once-in-a-lifetime experience where they can just be themselves, enjoy the time together before going back to work.They are really looking forward to it."The window is tight. The entire honeymoon is timed around Kelce's reporting date for Chiefs camp, so the couple will need to move fast and stay off the radar simultaneously.Kelce came close to walking away from football entirely after last season. He ultimately returned on a new three-year deal, and Patrick Mahomes made clear just how much that decision mattered to the locker room."Obviously, he has the physical gifts to go out there and be that size with that speed and looseness and catch the football," Mahomes told Yahoo Sports. "But I think what makes him who he is -- the leader and the person that he is -- the teammates around him want him to succeed because he's gonna give everything he has for the guys around him."Those words carry extra weight given what Kansas City is heading into. Last season was the first time in over a decade that the Chiefs missed the playoffs, and Mahomes is still rehabbing a torn ACL suffered in December. He is on track for Week 1, but no definitive timeline has been confirmed. Kelce returning healthy and motivated matters more now than it might have during the dynasty years.The honeymoon is the last stretch of calm before all of that begins.
Article Summary: Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift have kept things quiet since their July 3 wedding. The newlyweds are reportedly planning an ambitious around-the-world honeymoon. The honeymoon is timed around Kelce's reporting date for Chiefs camp.

Article Title: CBS NFL reporter Melanie Collins turns heads with a stylish golf course look while enjoying the offseason
Article Text:
CBS NFL reporter Melanie Collins turns heads with a stylish golf course look while enjoying the offseason(Getty)

NFL reporter Melanie Collins mixes style with an unforgettable Ballyhack Golf Club moment

Melanie Collins stylish golf look(Instagram)

The NFL offseason has given Melanie Collins a break from the sidelines, and she is making the most of it. The CBS Sports reporter recently caught fans' attention after sharing a stylish look from a day at Ballyhack Golf Club. Her post was not only about fashion. It also featured one of the closest moments of her golfing journey.Collins revealed she came within inches of her first career hole in one, turning a relaxing day on the course into a memorable one. The combination of a near-perfect shot and a sleek golf outfit quickly made the update a talking point among her followers.The popular NFL reporter Melanie Collins shared the update on Instagram from Ballyhack Golf Club, a private course in Virginia. She stepped onto the fairway in a coordinated black golf outfit that included a sleeveless cropped zip-up polo, a matching athletic skort, a black visor and black Nike golf shoes. The clean all-black look stood out as much as her game and drew plenty of attention from fans in the comments.The stylish outfit was not the only thing she spoke about. In the caption, Collins revealed she came heartbreakingly close to her first career hole-in-one. She wrote on Instagram, "This close to my first hole-in-one but hit the base of the pin and lipped out." While she did not share the shot itself, the update showed just how close she came to achieving one of golf's rarest milestonesGolf has become one of Collins' favourite offseason activities, offering a break from the busy NFL calendar before another season begins. Away from football, she often shares moments from the course, travels and outdoor adventures with her followers.Collins has worked as a CBS Sports NFL sideline reporter since joining the network in 2018. She regularly teams up with veteran play-by-play commentator Kevin Harlan and analyst Trent Green during NFL broadcasts. Before CBS, she built her broadcasting resume with Yahoo Sports and ESPN, covering events including the Super Bowl, FIFA World Cup, Winter Olympics and NBA coverage. She also studied sports journalism at Penn State University before beginning her television career.Collins has also become one of the most recognisable sideline reporters in the NFL because of her calm presence during live broadcasts and her ability to deliver updates under pressure. After completing her eighth season with CBS earlier this year, she thanked her colleagues and viewers on Instagram, calling herself grateful for another memorable year covering the league. This offseason has simply offered a different side of her routineWith the NFL season still weeks away, Collins appears to be enjoying every bit of her downtime. Her latest golf outing showed both her growing love for the sport and a polished sense of style, while the near hole-in-one gave fans another reason to follow along before she returns to the NFL sidelines this fall.
Article Summary: CBS NFL reporter Melanie Collins shared an Instagram update from Ballyhack Golf Club. She wore a stylish all-black outfit and came within inches of a hole-in- one. Collins has become one of the most recognisable sideline reporters in the NFL.

Article Title: "It’s almost impossible": Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader Emily Awbrey exposes the hidden struggle behind covering her tattoo
Article Text:
Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader Emily Awbrey explains how she covers her hand tattoo

Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders appearance rules remain unchanged

Making the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders squad takes far more than dance talent. Every detail matters, including appearance. Just days after earning a coveted spot on the 2026-27 roster, rookie Emily Awbrey pulled back the curtain on one of the beauty routines fans had been curious about for months, showing exactly how she hides her hand tattoo to meet the team's long-standing appearance standards.Emily Awbrey's journey to the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders has already become one of the most inspiring stories of the season. After falling short during last year's auditions, she returned determined to earn a place on the iconic squad and successfully secured a spot as one of the team's "comeback girls."Following the announcement, fans who watched America's Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders began asking the same question. How does she cover the hand tattoo that appeared during the Netflix series?Awbrey answered that curiosity herself in a detailed Instagram video, taking followers through every step of the process."I’ve gotten a lot of questions asking how I do it, so I thought I’d do a little video and show you how I cover it," she said.She admitted the process starts with an imperfect canvas because of a recent spray tan."I take this most disgusting, dusty, gross beauty blender that I only use for this," she joked before applying Dermablend leg and body makeup.Rather than piling on a thick coat immediately, Awbrey prefers building coverage gradually."Not a super heavy layer, because we’re going to double layer it," she explained, noting that blending makeup across the entire hand creates a more natural finish. She also works product into every crease by moving her fingers before locking everything in with loose setting powder.The rookie also shared one surprising confession.She told fans "a little secret," revealing that she does not always cover the tattoo on one finger because it is usually hidden by the team's pom-poms.Still, she admitted that concealing tattoos on hands is one of the hardest beauty challenges."It’s almost impossible" because her hands constantly move and rub together, making makeup difficult to keep in place.Awbrey's tutorial also highlighted the strict grooming standards that continue to define the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.According to the team's official guidelines, hopefuls may audition with tattoos, but no tattoo, regardless of size, can be visible while wearing the uniform or rehearsal attire. That rule has remained in place for decades alongside other appearance expectations covering hair, makeup and overall presentation.To improve the coverage, Awbrey applied another layer of foundation, additional powder and a darker shade that better matched her arm."I don’t think anyone knew I had a hand tattoo until the show came out," she said while demonstrating the final steps.She also warned that patience is essential during the routine."You’ve got to be careful because the more you touch, the more you pick up the foundation, because there’s just a lot of layer there … you can’t blend it too much, you kind of just have to let it low-key sit."After adding bronzer to balance the color from her spray tan, she finished everything with two setting sprays, calling the final step the key to keeping the makeup in place throughout practices and performances.Even then, Awbrey acknowledged the process is not flawless."Is it perfect? No. But it will get the job done, I’d say," she said.Her candid tutorial gave fans a rare behind the scenes look at the preparation required to meet one of professional cheerleading's most recognizable standards, proving that making the squad involves plenty of dedication long before stepping onto the field.
Article Summary: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader Emily Awbrey explains how she hides her hand tattoo. The team's appearance rules remain unchanged and no tattoo, regardless of size, can be visible while wearing the uniform or rehearsal attire. Her tutorial also highlighted the strict grooming standards that continue to define the team.
